The Ray County Commission addressed public comments and administrative operations. A local vendor pitched commercial HVAC services for future county projects. A resident raised Sunshine Law compliance questions regarding closed-session voting records and a recent cyber hack, which the commission declined to discuss. Commissioners also heard complaints regarding an unfixed roadside ditch and a disputed road district permit fee for emergency water line repairs. 

In official actions, the commission approved a resolution to advertise for an open Road and Bridge Secretary position and tabled a funding request for the Senior Center's phone system. Finally, they rejected current custodial bids, tabling the issue to rework contract specifications for a decision next week.

===== FULL DESCRIPTION =====

The Ray County Commission held a public meeting to address various administrative items, hear public comments, and vote on key resolutions. The session was called to order at 9:00 AM and recorded for the public record. 

**Public Comments**

**TempCon Presentation** 
Laura Chalk, representing TempCon—a commercial HVAC, plumbing, and refrigeration company—addressd the commission. Chalk noted that TempCon had bid on HVAC equipment for the Ray County Jail earlier in the year but was unsuccessful. She used her time to introduce the company’s wide range of services, which include installations for large commercial projects, preventative maintenance, and laboratory equipment calibrations. She emphasized TempCon’s customer-focused approach and highly competitive labor rates, noting a standard rate of $135 per hour, which drops to $120 per hour under a preventative maintenance agreement. The commission thanked her for the presentation and advised that future business opportunities would be announced through standard public notice channels, such as local newspapers and online postings.

**Sunshine Law and Cyberattack Inquiry** 
Local citizen Kirk Croy presented a Sunshine Law request regarding closed session voting records from 2025 and 2026. Croy questioned why no voting records were available for closed meetings related to personnel matters, speculating that this implied no county employees were hired, fired, or disciplined. The commission clarified that individual elected officeholders manage their own employees, and no formal votes were cast during the specific closed sessions in question. 

Croy then pivoted to a cyberattack the county experienced in 2025, asking if any county IT employees were fired or disciplined for the vulnerability. The commission firmly declined to discuss the matter, stating that the incident had been handled through proper legal channels and insurance attorneys. When Croy pressed the issue, he was warned that he would be removed from the meeting if he continued that line of questioning.

**Ditch Complaint** 
Croy also raised a recurring grievance regarding a large ditch near his driveway that is causing damage to his vehicle. He expressed frustration over the lack of action despite six months of complaints, noting that passing road graders have not addressed the issue. A commissioner agreed to follow up with the road district. Later in the meeting, the commissioner confirmed that a new machine designed specifically for ditch maintenance would be available in a couple of weeks. Croy agreed that this timeline was acceptable.

**Water District Permit Fee Dispute** 
Jesse Howe, representing Ray County District #2 Water, complained about a permit fee he was charged following an April 24th storm. A fallen tree rocked the ground hard enough to split a water main on West 84th Street. Howe hired Decker Construction to remove the tree while road district employees observed. He was subsequently charged a right-of-way permit fee to fix the water line. Howe argued that the fee was unjust, especially given previous instances where county roadwork had damaged water mains. The commission agreed to look into the specific incident and discuss the matter further with Planning and Zoning to see if a reimbursement or solution could be reached. 

**Ray County Senior Center Request** 
Brian Couch of the Ray County Senior Center requested funding for an upgraded phone system and a county cell phone. Couch explained that the center’s current landline system is severely antiquated and frequently drops calls. Furthermore, following a recent break-in, the center purchased internal cameras, but the administrator has to manage the system using his personal cell phone. The commission tabled the request, passing a voice vote to review the available funds and the specific responsibilities for the phone system before rendering a final decision.

**Administrative Business**

**Road and Bridge Secretary Resignation** 
The commission addressed the upcoming vacancy of the Road and Bridge Secretary, who is resigning to relocate to the northwest. To ensure a smooth transition, the commission read a resolution authorizing the immediate posting and advertisement of the job. The position will be posted on the official public board, the county website, and in local newspapers, with interviews anticipated during the first week of June 2026. The commission passed a motion to unanimously approve the resolution, expressing gratitude for the outgoing secretary’s two years of service to Ray County.

**Custodial Services Contract** 
The commission reviewed proposals for the county custodial contract. The bids came in significantly higher than the current budget. A point of confusion arose regarding the scope of work; the contractor had included the Public Administrator's office and increased service frequencies in the new bid based on informal conversations. The commission clarified that the current contract only covers the courthouse and Eagleton, and they wished to stick to those specific facilities. 

Additionally, the commission noted issues with the Public Administrator's trash being left out
